name: lief
why: A library for parsing and modifying ELF, PE and Mach-O binaries, a real door into instrumenting executables.

brief.what_it_is: LIEF is a cross-platform library that parses, inspects, modifies, and rebuilds executable files in ELF, PE, and Mach-O formats (and also COFF, DEX, and others, per the README). You feed it a binary file or an in-memory buffer and get back a structured object model with sections, symbols, relocations, and entry points, plus a shared abstraction across formats. You can change parts of that model, such as adding a section or renaming a symbol, and write a valid binary back to disk. The API is available in C++, Python, and Rust. The optional LIEF Extended tier adds disassembly, assembly, DWARF and PDB debug info, and Objective-C metadata.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a way to move from raw executable file formats to a high-level representation, make precise changes, and write a valid binary back, without booting a heavyweight reverse-engineering stack. The README frames the purpose as providing a cross-platform library to parse, modify and abstract ELF, PE and MachO formats.
brief.how_it_works: LIEF parses the file into a format-specific object model, and for ELF, PE, and Mach-O it also offers a common abstraction layer over shared concepts like sections, symbols, and entry points. Changes are made on that model, and format-aware builders serialize the result back to a file. The Extended tier layers disassembly and assembly (AArch64, x86/x86-64, ARM, RISC-V and others) on top of the same model.

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install of the LIEF package, listed under the Homebrew heading in the README.
Installs the latest released Python package from PyPI, per the README's Python section.
Installs a nightly Python build from the project's own index instead of PyPI. The bracketed --user flag is optional.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew (brew install lief) and pip (pip install lief) are the simplest routes. C++ projects use CMake with find_package(LIEF REQUIRED) and link LIEF::LIEF. Rust projects add lief = "1.0.0" to Cargo.toml. Nightly SDK and wheels come from a separate S3 index. The README links per-platform guides for Python, Visual Studio, Xcode, and CMake. LIEF Extended is distributed separately at extended.lief.re and requires GitHub OAuth sign-in. The README gives no runtime or account requirements for the core library.
brief.standout: One API spans three major executable formats, so the same concepts (sections, symbols, entry point) carry over between ELF, PE, and Mach-O. Compared with stacks that focus on analysis, LIEF is built for rewriting: the homepage's example patches an entry point and calls write, and its Extended demo disassembles an instruction, reassembles it as same-size NOPs, and rebuilds the ELF. It also ships a lief-patchelf reimplementation of NixOS patchelf and Ghidra and Binary Ninja plugins.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage announces LIEF 1.0.0 with a blog post dated Jul 13, 2026, and lists an earlier 0.17.0 release dated Sep 14, 2025 along with a lief-patchelf post from Jul 13, 2025. It also states 10+ years of continuous development and an active sponsor (Quansight). I did not see a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: Disassembly and assembly are part of LIEF Extended, not the open-source core; the homepage notes that the mutation and rebuild stages use the core API. Extended packages require GitHub OAuth. The README lists an unofficial, AI-generated Node.js binding (node-lief), which is not maintained by the project. The homepage's install-count and '1,000,000+ installs every month' figure is the project's own claim and I did not verify it. The BibTeX entry still points to the older lief.quarkslab.com address. The homepage example writes to a patched file and the README does not say it is safe on arbitrary binaries. Licensing: the core is Apache-2.0; I did not check the license terms for Extended.
quotes: Parse, inspect, modify, and build ELF, PE, Mach-O, and more through one consistent C++, Python, or Rust API.
Move from raw executable file formats to a high-level representation, make precise changes, then write a valid binary back to disk.
The purpose of this project is to provide a cross-platform library to parse, modify and abstract ELF, PE and MachO formats.

judge.reason: LIEF makes executable formats tangible: inspect and rewrite ELF, PE, and Mach-O binaries through one API, opening a compelling door into how programs are built.

entry.title: LIEF
entry.tldr: A library that parses, edits and rewrites ELF, PE and Mach-O executables through one API in C++, Python or Rust.
entry.deeper_look:
LIEF reads an executable file, or an in-memory buffer, and turns it into an object model: sections, symbols, relocations, an entry point. For ELF, PE and Mach-O it also offers a shared abstraction, so the same ideas carry across formats. You can change the model, for example by adding a section or renaming a symbol, and write a valid binary back to disk.

The homepage pitches this as a way to move "from raw executable file formats to a high-level representation, make precise changes, then write a valid binary back to disk", without booting a heavyweight reverse-engineering stack. Many tools focus on analysis. LIEF is built for rewriting.

The idea underneath is that an executable is just a structured file, and once you can see the structure you can edit it. Headers, section tables and symbol tables stop being mysterious. The project also ships lief-patchelf, a reimplementation of NixOS patchelf, plus Ghidra and Binary Ninja plugins.

A separate tier, LIEF Extended, adds disassembly, assembly, DWARF and PDB debug info, and Objective-C metadata. Its demo disassembles an instruction, reassembles it as same-size NOPs and rebuilds the ELF.
entry.install:
brew install lief
# the Homebrew formula installs the library and has no executables; for Python use: pip install lief

try_this.what_happens: Installs the LIEF library through Homebrew. It provides no command-line tools, so you use it from code.
Installs the Python package from PyPI, the quickest way to load a binary and look at its sections and symbols.
Installs a nightly Python build from the project's own index instead of PyPI.

entry.whats_unique: One API covers ELF, PE and Mach-O, and it is aimed at modifying and rebuilding binaries rather than only analysing them.
entry.caveats: The Homebrew formula installs no executables, so it is a library you write code against; disassembly and assembly live in LIEF Extended, which is distributed separately and requires GitHub OAuth sign-in.
